title: Scammers and spammers made marketing too challenging
author: EverythingBOffensive
selftext:
Nobody can trust anybody, on the internet or elsewhere of course but we used to not be as skeptic about whether someone was a bot, scammer, ai assistant, or if they are legit about making their sales and getting their name out there, networking.

Its going to keep getting worse. There will always be entities out there flooding the market with trash, slop, misleading spam, knockoffs, and shit that makes people rather rotate on a cactus than download your steamkey. we are fucked. nobody wants to play our games especially with the bad rep, its like, creating a bomb that does the opposite of destruction, but since bomb is in the name its BAD. thats our situation with AI right now, we are bad because people fucked it up before us.

How can we get out of this? Even if we don't use AI nobody will trust a new game dev anymore unless you have some kind of internet fame.

comments.author: Playistheway
comments.body: Yes, please keep that mindset. It ensures that I have one less competitor.

replies.author: EverythingBOffensive
replies.body: I wasn't implying that I was opting out of business. I was implying that you are ensured to have autonomous competitors controlled by people who can prevent consumers from seeing their competitors. The most promoted game ads on social media are from them for example. How do you counter that now?

replies.author: Playistheway
replies.body:
There has never been an easier time to market. 

For all of your doomerism, CAC hasn't materially changed. 

Storefronts like Steam have implemented long overdue personalised recommender algorithms. You're now a lot more likely to get warm leads before launch.

You can generate capsule art to split test 100 different pieces of capsule art in an hour. 

You can create a mailing list, and a Discord server in a few clicks to gain control over your audience.

You can automate the process of taking Git commits and turn them into brand appropriate marketing material, using tried-and-true copywriting frameworks.

There are people who will professionally 'clip' video from your game and get paid per view.

95% of marketing is building a product that the market wants. Marketing begins at idea generation. 

If you're struggling to find a market for your game, it's ultimately just a skill issue. There is nothing stopping any of us from making a billion dollar game, except ignorance debt.

You're cooked if you are entitled and ignorant. You're printing money if you're willing to pay down your ignorance debt.

comments.author: Apalala__
comments.body:
Looks like the only thing to trust is AI.  
Though we should have taken into account that AI did not just make games easier,  
It made everything else easier such as marketing.

You have to do more to stand out.

comments.author: faseer
comments.body: Are you saying that the emergence of AI has made distrust easier, but it doesn't help in building trust at all?
